articles.title: Bombazo en Milán: Navarro y Di Nenno, fuera en octavos
articles.standfirst: La pareja cinco cayó eliminada ante una versión superlativa de Javi Garrido y Juani De Pascual, mientras que el resto de favoritas apenas sufrieron para meterse en cuartos.
articles.summary: La pareja cinco cayó eliminada ante una versión superlativa de Javi Garrido y Juani De Pascual, mientras que el resto de favoritas apenas sufrieron para meterse en cuartos.
articles.body: La pareja cinco masculina cierra una gira europea negra que comenzaron desde la cuarta posición en Rotterdam y acaban con una dura derrota en octavos del Milano P1. Porque la gran sorpresa del día llegaría al final de la jornada en la pista uno donde Juani de Pascual y Javi Garrido eliminarían por 6-2 y 6-3 a Di Nenno y Navarro a la séptima opción de partido. Una victoria que llega tras quedarse a las puertas de eliminar a Chingalán en Alemania y que esta semana sí ha dado la pareja decimosexta en unos octavos de final sin mayor susto para los cabezas de serie. De Pascual y Garrido, que comenzaron su andadura como equipo hace pocas semanas en el FIP Gold de Perugia donde cayeron en octavos y sin las mejores sensaciones, han conseguido revertir el inicio en la gira europea dando sentido a su unión y alcanzando ya los cuartos en Italia con un juego compacto, muy vertical y que no permitiría a sus rivales dominar en ningún momento. Un triunfo que tiene valor doble para Garrido pues, el español, supone la primera vez que consigue imponerse en el cruzado a Paquito Navarro ya que hasta el partido de Milán el cara a cara entre ambos era claramente favorable para el sevillano por 15 victorias y ninguna derrota. Una jornada la del jueves en la que tanto Tapia y Coello como Sanz y Stupaczuk arrollarían a sus rivales clavando el mismo resultado por 6-2 y 6-2 a sus rivales para medirse el viernes a Guerrero y Leal, los Golden Boys, y Momo González y Lucas Campagnolo los finalistas de las dos últimas citas. Jornada en la que también estarán Chingalán y Lebrón-Augsburger, parejas dos y tres del ranking, que lograrían avanzar cómodamente en los octavos de final y miran ya de reojo para citarse en semifinales en un encuentro que podría definir, en caso de darse, el número uno de la temporada. Además, en cuartos de final volverá a estar una de las parejas que mejor encara el tramo final de temporada como son los argentinos Tino Libaak y Gonza Alfonso que derrotarían a una pareja circuntancial como Yanguas y Lijó por 6-1 y 7-6.

articles.title: Opaque selection, forced doubles pairing: Para-shuttlers challenge Para Asian Games non-selection in Delhi HC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Chirag Baretha is a two-time Asian Games medallist, having won silver in 2023 and bronze in 2018.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Chirag Baretha is a two-time Asian Games medallist, having won silver in 2023 and bronze in 2018. Instead of focusing on the upcoming Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, which begin on October 18, he is running from pillar to post, trying to keep his fading dream of representing India alive. The 29-year-old has also won bronze medals at the 2024 BWF Para Badminton World Championships, the 2025 Asian Para Badminton Championships, and the 2026 World Para Badminton Championships.Baretha, alongside fellow para-shuttlers Shashank Kumar, Ammu Mohan and Manisha Patel, has filed a petition in the Delhi High Court against the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS), the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI), the Badminton Association of India (BAI) and the Sports Authority of India (SAI) over their non-selection.In the petition, accessed by TimesofIndia.com, the para-shuttlers argue that they meet the selection criteria set by the Sports Ministry, which require them to be ranked in the top six in Asia. Baretha and Mandeep Kaur were ranked World No. 6 in the SL3-SU5 category on July 14, 2026, when the rankings were considered for the Asian Para Games.Subsequently, the petition argues that "Rakesh Pandey has not obtained or won any medal in the last 12 months or have ranking less than the petitioners in the international athlete ranking. Moreover, he was debarred for 4 years for failing the Anti-Doping Test."The men's doubles pairing of Rakesh Pandey and Dev Rathi was ranked World No. 3 in the SU5 category on the cutoff date. However, Rakesh is set to partner Umesh Vikram Kumar in men's doubles at the Asian Para Games, while also finding a spot in the men's singles discipline.This, too, has a layer of intrigue. In an email sent to qualified para-shuttlers on August 25, K Prabhakar Rao, the chairman of para-badminton at the Badminton Association of India (BAI), made it clear that "for a pair to be considered valid for recommendation, separate emails must be received from both players, with each player naming the other as their partner for the concerned event."In response, Baretha, who was named in the Badminton World Federation's (BWF) entry list, registered for singles (SU5 category), men's doubles (SU5 with Hardik Makkar) and mixed doubles (SL3-SU5 with Mandeep Kaur).However, Vikram, Pandey's partner at the Asian Para Games, expressed displeasure at his name being added to the doubles draw without his consent. "Sir, I have not given consent to participate in MD SL3 SU5. How can I [sic] my name appear in doubles? Please make sure to remove my name from doubles without affecting my singles entry," he wrote in a WhatsApp group for Asian Para Games athletes. He addressed the message to Prabhakar Rao and coach Venkata Murali Krishna.However, his plea was not entertained. "Vikram, we can discuss this in a physical meeting at hotel. At this stage, no modification is allowed. We already discussed with referee, ABC [Asian Badminton Confederation] persons."Not satisfied, Vikram responded, "Sir, I will be arriving at hotel late tonight and by that time draw will be announced. Without my consent, my name should not be entered. Pandey bhaiya can play with Hardik (Makkar)."For Vikram, there is no way out. The rules stipulate that if a player withdraws from one discipline, they withdraw from the entire tournament.We are fighting on a merit basis. We are medal holders. We are rank holders. We followed the guidelines of SAI. But Mr Prabhakar Rao has tricked us and affected our career and effort of four years.This sequence of events, and the eventual loss of his place in the contingent, has left Baretha distraught."We are (fighting) on a merit basis. We are medal holders. We are rank holders. We followed the guidelines of SAI. But Mr Prabhakar Rao has tricked us and affected our career and effort of four years," Baretha told TimesofIndia.com."I am Asia No. 6 and have qualified through my ranking. Even if you ignore that, I meet another clause of being a medallist from previous Games. The same applied to Suhas (Lalinakere Yathiraj), who was not in the top six but had won a medal the last time [gold]."The Badminton Association of India didn't have a say in this. We didn't include or exclude an athlete as per our choices. We got this list from SAI, and we followed it."Before my name was withdrawn at the manager's meeting, the draw was such that I was destined to reach the final. Except for one player, I have been able to beat everyone. I could guarantee the country a silver medal," he added confidently.K Prabhakar Rao said the squad selection was not theirs to make in the first place."The Badminton Association of India didn't have a say in this. We didn't include or exclude an athlete as per our choices. We got this list from SAI, and we followed it," he told TimesofIndia.com.The exclusion of former head coach Gaurav Khanna is believed to have been a major factor in the entire selection fracas. Khanna, who established India's first para-badminton academy (Gaurav Khanna Excellia Badminton Academy), has the likes of Suhas and Baretha under his wing.Baretha alleged that senior para-shuttlers were instrumental in creating a negative impression of Khanna among officials at SAI. "These senior athletes have set a wrong aura in front of the Sports Authority of India. They have also harmed me. It includes Sukant Kadam, Nitesh Kumar, Pramod Bhagat and Rakesh Pandey himself.""They keep going on about the academy, but at least look at my credentials. Look at my medals, my ranking. I am talking about my achievements."In the days following the squad announcement and Baretha's omission on October 12, Baretha, Shashank Kumar and Ammu Mohan approached the Delhi High Court and met Dr Pallavi Rai, SAI's director (TEAMS Division), but failed to receive a satisfactory response. Their repeated attempts to seek clarity from BAI secretary Sanjay Mishra and K Prabhakar Rao have also failed to yield results.The para-shuttlers are not the only aggrieved group of Indian athletes. Para-shooters and para-cyclists, too, had demanded a fairer and more transparent selection process. They held a protest during the send-off ceremony on October 8.India has sent a 281-member contingent to the Asian Para Games, which includes 168 athletes.SEQUENCE OF EVENTSSeptember 24, 2025: The Sports Ministry issues selection criteria for the Asian Games and Asian Para Games.October 2026: BAI reiterates the selection criteria for the Asian Para Games.October 12: SAI announces the contingent for the Asian Para Games.October 13: Para-shuttlers converge in Delhi to travel to the Games.October 13: Chirag Baretha, Shashank Kumar, Ammu Mohan and Manisha Patel file a petition in the Delhi High Court over their non-selection.October 14: Para-shuttlers report in Aichi-Nagoya.October 16: Badminton begins at the Asian Para Games.October 18: The Asian Para Games are officially opened.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers end the Dodgers’ quest for a third-straight title, sweeping LA to earn a trip to the World Series
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are headed to the World Series after a dominating sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers, the reigning two-time champions.
articles.body: Major League Baseball will have a new champion this fall. The Milwaukee Brewers are headed to the World Series after a dominating sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers, the reigning two-time champions. The high-priced Dodgers aimed to make history as the first National League team to ever win three straight titles, but Shohei Ohtani and company ran into a blue-and-yellow buzzsaw this week. Milwaukee pulled off a four-game sweep of the Dodgers, capping their domination with a 6-4 victory at Dodger Stadium on Thursday. “We’re just happy for our fans, for everybody that’s been a part of this organization and stuck with us over the years,” captain Christian Yelich said after the game. “We’ve come close a bunch of times to get to this point. We’ve still got a ways to go, we still got some big games in front of us.” The Brewers were baseball’s best team in the regular season and were looking for revenge after the Dodgers swept them in dominant fashion on their way to the 2025 title. This year, it’s the Dodgers who are left wondering what just happened and the Brewers going on to pull off a bit of history: The Brew Crew are looking for their organization’s first title and Milwaukee has only been to the Fall Classic once in team history, losing in seven games in 1982. In front of a stunned Dodgers Stadium, the Brewers fought back on Thursday from an early 4-0 deficit. Ohtani seemed to shake off months of doldrums, hitting a three-run home run in the second inning that put the defending champs up with a big lead. Sometimes in the playoffs, a four-run lead can feel like more than enough. But the Brewers were not fazed by Ohtani’s jubilant celebration after his moonshot and began to chip away. The Brewers scored two runs in the fourth and two more in the fifth to tie the game. Then it was center fielder Garrett Mitchell who hit a long drive to deep right field in the sixth, carrying the fence and landing in the first row of seats, that gave Milwaukee the lead. Mitchell’s blast seemed to knock some of the fight out of the Dodgers, who were able to get the tying run to third base three times in the ensuing innings but couldn’t quite get the big hit needed to even the contest. The subdued crowd in Chavez Ravine was often drowned out by the paltry number of Brewers fans in attendance. Their best chance came in the bottom of the eighth when longtime catcher Will Smith laced the ball into the right field corner. It bounced around, eluding Brewers right fielder Sal Frelick and Smith was able to get to third with a stand-up triple. There was just one out and the Dodgers’ latest expensive signing, Kyle Tucker, coming up next. Tucker was jammed by an Aaron Ashby pitch, flying out to short center field for the second out. Teoscar Hernández followed, looking to author yet another signature playoff moment for the Dodgers. It never came – instead Hernández was left baffled by an Ashby curveball, striking out and stranding Smith. Ashby, who pitched the final three innings of the game, said he felt very calm on the mound. “I think I was just praying for a little peace in the chaos. Because with this crowd, with this team, things can happen fast. I guess just trying to be calm and felt a lot of peace out there,” he told the Fox broadcast. Just an inning later, David Hamilton added an insurance run, belting a solo home run to make it 6-4 in the top of the ninth. It was a strange way for this dominant run for the Dodgers to end, a comparative whimper after two years of massive success. LA had long been expected to waltz to another title with the game’s second-most-expensive roster paired with the kind of analytics baseball has embraced over the last two decades. Instead, it will be the comparatively thrifty Brewers representing the National League in the World Series, which promises to be a battle of the little guys. The Brewers’ roster cost about $143 million to assemble, good for 19th in MLB this year. They’ll play either the Cleveland Guardians or Tampa Bay Rays, two of the cheapest teams in the league. The Guardians payroll is the lowest in the league at $74 million; the Rays are 25th at $98 million. After being swept by the Dodgers last year, it was a moment of catharsis for the Brewers and their fans. “You don’t ever know what to expect coming into a series like that last year. You don’t know how bad it could be and then it was as bad as it was,” Ashby said. “We came out and we survived, and we came back this year and those guys played their tails off. I’d die for any of these dudes”

articles.title: Less than 2 years after coaching college hoops in Florida, Karl Smesko leads Atlanta Dream to WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Karl Smesko left Florida Gulf Coast's beach campus after eight 30-win seasons to chase the title he could never win there with the Atlanta Dream.
articles.body: Karl Smesko enjoyed notable success during his time coaching the Florida Gulf Coast women’s basketball team. But rather than remain at the college level, where he had built a powerhouse at FGCU, Smesko chose in pursue a new challenge in the WNBA. When Smesko arrived at FGCU, the program competed in Division II. By the time he left to become the next head coach of the Atlanta Dream, the Eagles had established themselves as one of the premier programs in Division I women’s basketball. Under Smesko, FGCU routinely led the nation in 3-pointers made. The Eagles also recorded eight 30-win seasons and advanced to the NCAA tournament 10 times with Smesko at the helm, but he never captured the ultimate prize: an NCAA Division I championship. Perhaps the call about the opportunity in Atlanta came at just the right time for Smesko. He may have accomplished nearly everything possible at FGCU, effectively reaching the program's ceiling. ATLANTA DREAM ADVANCE TO WNBA PLAYOFFS SEMIFINALS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2018 WITH GAME 2 WIN Perhaps Smesko realized that his long-sought dream of hoisting a championship trophy would require him to step outside his comfort zone and take a chance with the actual Dream at the professional basketball level. So far, Smesko’s gamble has worked out. He has guided Atlanta to back-to-back 30-win seasons, and after a first-round exit last year, the Dream have swept their first two opponents in the 2026 postseason to reach the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. The championship he was never going to get at FGCU is now four wins away, with the title series against the favored Golden State Valkyries set to begin on Saturday. "As good as we were at Florida Gulf Coast, the odds were very stacked against us to make that type of championship run," Smesko said. "In the pros, I definitely thought there was more of an opportunity. It’s a more equal playing field to win the whole thing and that was appealing to me." GOLDEN STATE VALKYRIES ERASE 16-POINT DEFICIT, STUN DALLAS WINGS TO REACH WNBA SEMIFINALS The 2026 Finals will feature a matchup of second-year coaches: Smesko in Atlanta and Natalie Nakase in Golden State, which is in just its second year of existence. The Valkyries went 3-0 against the Dream this season, making them just the second team to sweep Smesko’s club in his tenure there. But in Smesko the Dream trust. "He’s a coach that really believes in you and he knows what’s best," Dream star Angel Reese said. "And I’m really thankful for him, for being able to help me with my career and help me be better for the team — because I don’t think I would be in this situation and thriving as I am individually without him." Smesko is quiet in many ways, and fiercely loyal. The offer from the Dream came as FGCU was starting its 2024-25 season; he wound up leaving after two games that year, though some at the school believe he was tempted to try to handle both jobs at once for a few months and finish that season. He ended up turning the keys to FGCU over to longtime top assistant Chelsea Lyles. She ended up following in her mentor’s footsteps, winning 30 games and taking the Eagles to the NCAA Tournament. articles.title: China’s stapled visa row costs Arunachal weightlifter shot at World Championships
articles.summary: New Delhi: Another sporting flashpoint in India-China ties has cost weightlifter Charu Pesi a shot at the world stage, with the Indian Weightlifting
articles.body: New Delhi: Another sporting flashpoint in India-China ties has cost weightlifter Charu Pesi a shot at the world stage, with the Indian Weightlifting Federation (IWLF) withdrawing the Arunachal Pradesh athlete from the upcoming Senior World Weightlifting Championships in Ningbo after Chinese authorities indicated that he would be issued a stapled visa.Sources told TOI that the Chinese Visa Application Service Centre (CVASS) here sought an undertaking from the Indian federation confirming Pesi’s acceptance of the visa.The IWLF consulted government officials, who maintained that India does not recognise stapled visas issued by China to residents of Arunachal Pradesh. The federation subsequently decided against sending the men’s 65kg lifter to the championships, which begin on Oct 24.An eight-member Indian squad, led by Olympic medallist Mirabai Chanu, is scheduled to compete in Ningbo, with visa processing for the rest of the contingent continuing as usual.Unlike a regular visa stamped on a passport, a stapled visa is issued on a separate piece of paper. Beijing’s practice of issuing such visas to Arunachal Pradesh residents reflects its refusal to recognise India’s sovereignty over the region. India has consistently rejected the practice, viewing it as a challenge to its territorial integrity.This is far from an isolated incident. In July 2023, three Arunachal Pradesh wushu athletes, Nyeman Wangsu, Onilu Tega and Mepung Lamgu, were issued stapled visas for the Summer World University Games in Chengdu. India protested and withdrew its entire wushu contingent.The dispute resurfaced ahead of the Hangzhou Asian Games later that year, when the athletes faced entry and accreditation hurdles, preventing them from competing.For the lifter, it is a bitter setback. articles.title: Sonipat’s golden harvest: How Haryana city became India’s medal factory
articles.summary: When Kushal Dalal picked up boxing gloves, his family didn’t say no.
articles.body: When Kushal Dalal picked up boxing gloves, his family didn’t say no. When he gave that up and decided on archery – because Kushal didn’t like the idea of hitting anyone and felt at home in “a peaceful sport” – they agreed to that, too. There was no place around to practise archery, so a section of the family’s 5-acre farmland at Siwanka village in Sonipat was cleared. Paddy straw was woven to give him targets.Village gossip had brought Kiran Pahal’s running days to an abrupt end. After talk of Kiran “speaking to a boy” reached her father, he stopped her from going out. He relented after Kiran went on a hunger strike. Her grandmother used money from her pension to buy her a pair of running shoes.Before Neha Goyal played hockey for India, she helped her mother and sisters fix bicycles. Neha was eight when a friend told her hockey players got free shoes, clothes and notebooks. Her mother, who worked in houses and at a foam factory, didn’t stop her from playing.At the recently concluded Asian Games in Japan’s Aichi-Nagoya, a neighbour of Delhi reaped possibly India’s biggest harvest for a single city. Each of these stories – and 10 more like these – culminated in a gold medal. Each began, and blossomed, in Sonipat.0b38c222-aa4e-4223-b642-92ec90d3a2a3Though in NCR, Sonipat doesn’t have Delhi’s influence, Gurgaon’s money or Noida’s infrastructure. As a manufacturing hub of auto components and ancillaries that are used in the domestic market and abroad, Sonipat has so far been writing its script, literally, in parts.Sport, which bubbles in its DNA, works much in the same way – many individual parts that don’t get to show their prowess as a sum. Aichi-Nagoya was that rare instance when they did. Serendipity? Perhaps. Organisation? Possible. Talent? Certainly.But talent needs spotting. And for virtually all the gold medallists, that was someone in the family who made it possible, sometimes with a push, sometimes with a quiet sacrifice –a family clearing land, a grandmother spending her pension, a mother working to buy shoes, a coach paying school fees for a stranger’s daughter.The other aspect of the Japan feat that places Sonipat apart from traditional sporting nurseries like Bhiwani (boxing) is the diversity of the 13 (individual and team combined) gold medals that athletes from here won, across disciplines like hockey, archery, kabaddi, athletics and wrestling.Serendipity did play a part. For several of these medallists, sport wasn’t the original dream. Neha Goyal, midfielder in the gold-winning women’s hockey team, started going for hockey classes after a friend told her hockey players received free shoes, clothes and notebooks. She joined because her family needed those things. Some families saw sport as a way to support the child’s education; others came to see it as a route eventually to a govt job.Coaches TOI spoke to said access to proper training remains the difference between a talent lost and a talent realised. Sonipat’s sportspersons have certainly benefited from its concentration of sports institutions and training centres around Rai and Bahalgarh. It has a Sports Authority of India (SAI) National Centre of Excellence, a residential sports school and Sports University of Haryana. The SAI centre covers 83 acres and its listed facilities include a 70-metre archery field, a floodlit synthetic athletics track, synthetic hockey fields, two mud kabaddi courts, wrestling halls, a sports injury and rehabilitation centre, a hypoxic chamber and hostels.Motilal Nehru School of Sports at Rai, founded by Haryana govt in 1973, has athletics, archery, weightlifting, wrestling and swimming among its competencies.Village akharas, kabaddi nurseries and private academies sit in different parts of the access route. One such academy, run by former India hockey captain Pritam Rani Siwach and her husband, has produced a steady stream of national hockey players. Seven hockey players from Sonipat were part of the men’s and women’s Indian teams that won gold at Aichi-Nagoya: four women and three men. All four women and one in the men’s team (Pritam Rani’s son Yashdeep) trained at the academy, which now has around 200 players, 150 of them girls.Among the youngest there is Ritika. The five-year-old is still mastering her numbers and alphabets in school but is quickly picking up dribbling and promptly agreed to show this reporter the right grip for the hockey stick. “Aise pakadte hain. Aur phir ball ko goal mein daalna hota hai. Jo ball andar daalega, woh jeetega! (this is how you hols the stick. The objective is to score a goal with the ball. Whoever does that wins)” she said.When Pritam Rani started the academy in 2004, she had seven trainees. When the academy paid school fees and helped buy shoes and other equipment, more began to join. I never wanted money to become the reason a talented girl stopped playing,” she told TOI. Food mattered, too. Many girls came from families for whom milk and fruit were luxuries, so the academy began providing soaked chana, milk and bananas.Neha, who came for the shoes, stayed for the dream – of building a house for her mother. “I did not start playing hockey thinking I wanted to play for India. I was in Class IV when a friend told me about the shoes, clothes and notebooks,” she said. “There were people who told my mother to keep me at home. But she never stopped me.” A cash prize for being player of the match changed her attitude towards hockey. “That Rs 2,000 changed something inside me. I started thinking if I played well, I could earn. Then on, hockey was not just a game for me. It became my responsibility,” she said.Abhishek Nain’s first reason for playing hockey was less ambitious. He was nine when he followed a classmate to a ground because it was an excuse to bunk. His father, who was with BSF, asked him to consider quitting hockey – which he was playing at the national level – after a series of injuries and focus on getting a govt job. Coaches persuaded the family to let him continue. Years later, at Aichi-Nagoya, he would score India’s winning goal against Pakistan in the Asiad semi-final.Seeing girls running on a track outside her school drew Kiran into athletics so much that she began sprinting in her school shoes and slippers, sometimes even barefoot. “I did not know where this would take me or that I would one day be wearing the India badge. I just liked running and wanted to try.” She joined Indian Railways in 2021, gaining financial stability after years of training. “For an athlete, knowing that there is a secure job gives a lot of confidence,” said Kiran, who won the 4x400m relay team gold in Japan.Meenu Beniwal, president of Haryana Olympic Association, linked Sonipat’s sporting culture to shrinking landholdings and search for livelihoods beyond farming. “As ancestral landholdings have shrunk and farming has become less viable for many families, sports have emerged as an important pathway to secure govt jobs and build a better future,” she said. Proximity to Delhi and recruitment opportunities in the Army, Railways, paramilitary forces and other central government departments have also encouraged young people to pursue sport, she felt.Sports University of Haryana vice-chancellor Ashok Kumar said ambitious parents have helped build the ecosystem by investing their own money and taking risks for their children. Institutions have added to that support, creating a baseline sporting infrastructure framework in the city. The university admits 1,000-plus students each year, and Sonipat accounts for around 20% of admissions.Kabaddi player Pardeep Narwal says children in villages such as Rindhana grow up watching neighbours, relatives and seniors succeed in the sport. Local grounds and kabaddi academies run by former players bring large numbers of youngsters into the sport. In Rindhana alone, around 300 children practise across three grounds, he said.“From my village alone 25-30 athletes have played in Pro Kabaddi League,” Narwal said. Seeing other athletes succeed encourages more children in the village to try. “Family members motivate the kids. They look at a neighbour’s son succeeding and ask their own children why they can’t do the same,” he said.Wrestler Naveen Mor describes the same process in akharas, with local dangals giving children competitive experience early. “When an entire community encourages a sport, the chances of producing champions naturally increase,” said Mor, who runs a wrestling academy on a one-acre plot near Murthal, where he trains 70-80 children. He said he does not charge them because talent may emerge from families unable to afford expensive coaching.“Many of our athletes come from humble farming families, where children grow up helping with physical work and learn discipline, endurance and the value of hard work early in life. Wrestling also offered generations of youngsters from middle-class families a way to build a career, earn recognition and secure a govt job. Earlier, choices for many such families were limited, and sports became a route to a better future. Over time, this created a strong sporting culture, with akharas, coaches, families and former wrestlers all contributing to the next generation,” Mor said.The same may now be happening for hockey and athletics. articles.title: Three Jharkhand players in India squad for historic lawn bowls series against New Zealand
articles.summary: Kolkata: Three players from Jharkhand will be part of India’s four-member lawn bowls squad for a historic three-Test series against New Zealand in Nov,
articles.body: Kolkata: Three players from Jharkhand will be part of India’s four-member lawn bowls squad for a historic three-Test series against New Zealand in Nov, part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two countries.Lawn bowls is one of the only four sports, alongside cricket, hockey and football, selected for the centenary programme.2022 Commonwealth Games silver medallists Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur and rising player Reshma Kumari, all from Jharkhand, have been selected alongside Arjuna Awardee and Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki Singh for the series, scheduled from Nov 16-18 in Auckland.“This is a very important event for us because only four sports are taking part in the centenary celebrations. On the days we are playing, no other sport will be taking place, which means we will receive exclusive coverage,” Bowling Federation of India president Ravi Bengani told TOI in an exclusive interview on Thursday.India will play three Test matches over three days, with each Test comprising five matches — men’s pairs, women’s pairs, mixed fours, mixed pairs 1 and mixed pairs 2.The New Zealand series is part of a broader international exposure programme the federation has put in place as it begins preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.A 12-member Indian contingent will travel to Malaysia later this month for a World Bowls-sanctioned tournament, while another group will compete in an invitational event in Hong Kong, where Indian players won bronze medals last year.The federation’s confidence has also received a boost from Putul Sonowal’s recent podium finish at the Champion of Champions event, a first for an Indian player at the prestigious competition.“We have decided to participate in as many World Bowls-sanctioned events as possible. International exposure is crucial if we want to bridge the gap with the leading nations,” Bengani said.The federation is also planning to strengthen its support structure through its partnership with Bowls New Zealand. Bengani revealed that India currently does not have a dedicated national coach, making the proposed knowledge-sharing programme particularly significant.“We have signed an agreement with Bowls New Zealand and now we will have more exchange programmes. We will bring their coaches and technical officials to India and provide our players with greater exposure and expertise,” Bengani said.The plans have gained momentum following the federation’s recognition by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports earlier this year, a move expected to improve funding and access to high-performance support.As far as the 2030 Commonwealth Games are concerned, the federation has set ambitious targets. “I’m committing to at least four gold medals for India in 2030. articles.title: La última vuelta de tuerca de Ray Zapata para volver al podio
articles.standfirst: El subcampeón olímpico de gimnasia artística explica a MARCA cómo se ha estado preparando en Panamá bajo las órdenes de Carlos Gil de cara al Mundial y en el camino a los Juegos
articles.summary: El subcampeón olímpico de gimnasia artística explica a MARCA cómo se ha estado preparando en Panamá bajo las órdenes de Carlos Gil de cara al Mundial y en el camino a los Juegos
articles.body: Ray Zapata tenía claro que debía salir de su zona de confort para avanzar. Después de años entrenando en el Centro de Alto Rendimiento de Madrid, el subcampeón olímpico de gimnasia artística (Tokio 2020) necesitaba un cambio. "Buscaba dar una vuelta de tuerca a mi última etapa deportiva para conseguir mejores resultados. Quiero volver al podio y para ello necesitaba un entrenador en consonancia", explica a MARCA. Y ese entrenador es el cubano Carlos Gil al que Zapata conoció en el Mundial de 2015. En aquella cita, en la que el español logró un bronce en suelo, el cubano Manrique Larduet debutó con una plata en el concurso completo individual. Sólo fue superado por la leyenda japonesa Kohei Uchimura, triple campeón olímpico y diez veces oro mundial. "Gil es el único entrenador del mundo que ha conseguido hacer frente a Japón", dice el gimnasta español. Su filosofía de entrenamiento se centra en la disciplina, el esfuerzo constante y el aprendizaje continuo. En la actualidad es el entrenador del equipo femenino panameño, por eso desde enero Ray ha ha pasado cuatro estancias de mes y medio en Panamá entrenando bajo sus órdenes. En esta nueva aventura cuenta con el respaldo de la Federación Española de Gimnasia. El trabajo ha empezado a dar sus frutos. Zapata actualmente es cuarto del ranking mundial. Fue bronce en la Copa del Mundo de Antalya (Turquía). "Hacía tiempo que no subía al podio. Me demuestra que puedo volver a estar entre los mejores", dice con confianza. Ha estado entrenando bajo las órdenes de Gil en el club NoLimits ubicado en Ciudad de Panamá. "Allí hacemos sesiones más largas de entrenamiento que requieren un esfuerzo extra, pero me está yendo bien", reconoce. Entrenaba doble sesión, mañana y tarde. Y no sólo se ha centrado en el suelo, su especialidad, también está mejorando en el salto. "No quiero cerrarme ninguna puerta. Voy a hacer dos saltos bastante potentes y puedo pelear en el Mundial por estar en la final de salto también", asegura. Ray debuta en el Campeonato del Mundo el 18 de octubre. Aunque ha estado trabajando con Gil en el Zapata III, no lo presentará en el Mundial. En el Europeo de este año se lesionó el bíceps izquierdo preparando las anillas para aportar nota para el equipo. "En el Mundial tengo un ejercicio bastante potente. No puedo arriesgarme a presentar nuevos elementos porque no puedo fallar y quedarme fuera de la final. El objetivo es pelear por las medallas", dice. Por eso, lo presentará en alguna Copa del Mundo. Su nuevo elemento consiste en un doble en carpa -dos saltos mortales consecutivos en el aire manteniendo el cuerpo doblado por la cadera con las piernas estiradas y juntas- hacia adelante con giro completo, añadiendo medio giro más del que se hace en la actualidad. "Es muy bonito pero muy fallón, ya se ha intentado antes. Quiero aportar una habilidad más a la gimnasia, que con el código de puntuación nuevo es un poco aburrida. Tanto el conocimiento de Carlos como las capacidades que he ido desarrollando con él lo hace más posible", dice con convicción. Entre los logros más recientes de Gil está el haber conseguido que la panameña Hillary Heron fuese la primera gimnasta en replicar el complicado 'Biles I' de suelo en un Campeonato del Mundo, un doble mortal extendido hacia atrás con medio giro. Porque Zapata, que trabaja con el psicólogo deportivo Pablo del Río desde hace años, quiere seguir innovando y explorando sus límites hasta la próxima cita olímpica, la cuarta en su haber. Estar lejos de su mujer y sus dos hijos es el alto peaje que está pagando para lograrlo y es lo que peor lleva. "Los Ángeles 2028 serán mis últimos Juegos Olímpicos. Quizá luego haga algún Mundial, pero no creo que vaya a estar mucho más tiempo. Sería muy mayor y sería forzar la máquina y si no voy a luchar por una medalla...", explica. Porque Ray no ha perdido con los años ni un ápice de su ambición.

articles.title: LIVE | Verstappen in action during first practice in Portimão
articles.summary: Max Verstappen continues his GT3 weekend in Portimão on Friday with the first free practice session. Following a promising test day, Mercedes-AMG Team Versta...
articles.body:
Max Verstappen continues his GT3 weekend in Portimão on Friday with the first free practice session. Following a promising test day, Mercedes-AMG Team Verstappen Racing will have another hour and a half to fine-tune its preparations. The session starts at 09:45 CEST and can be watched for free via the official livestream.

Verstappen is sharing the No. 3 Mercedes-AMG GT3 with Chris Lulham and Ben Barnicoat this weekend. The trio is preparing for the three-hour season finale of the GT World Challenge Europe Endurance Cup, which takes place on Saturday. But first, Friday brings a full day of action: both free practice sessions and qualifying are on the schedule.

Verstappen Racing gets off to a strong start in testing

GPblog followed the opening running in Portimão on Thursday. During the paid test session, running was temporarily neutralised with a Full Course Yellow in the first half-hour. This was prompted by Aliaksandr Malykhin spinning in the Pure Rxcing Porsche . For Verstappen Racing, the session was primarily an opportunity to work on the setup and assess how the Mercedes behaved over longer runs.

The team ultimately ended the test in second place. Lulham set the team's fastest lap, a 1:43.076, around a tenth of a second off the No. 17 GetSpeed Mercedes. The No. 3 car completed 43 laps without any issues. Barnicoat drove the opening stint before handing over to Lulham, with Verstappen taking the wheel for the final part of the two-hour session.

The first outing therefore provided a useful foundation. As noted on Thursday, the undulating circuit demands more than just engine power. Its elevation changes, blind corners and long, sweeping turns put the balance and tyres to the test. Finding a setup that all three drivers feel confident with is therefore important for the race. The practice sessions provide an opportunity to refine it further.

GT World Challenge Europe schedule in Portimão

The first free practice session runs until 11:15 CEST. The second session and qualifying follow later on Friday. The schedule is listed below, including the test session that has already taken place. All times are Dutch time; Portugal is one hour behind.

The first free practice session is available to watch for free via the official GT World broadcast. Watch the action via the GT World Challenge Europe livestream and follow Verstappen and his teammates as they prepare for the season finale in Portugal. You can also follow the Verstappen Racing trio on board. Watch the livestream here .

articles.title: Vatikiotis, Lenderman lead All Saints to 4th straight district title
articles.summary: Top-seeded All Saints pulls out tight third set and goes on to defeat Tampa Bay HEAT to capture the Class 1A, District 9 volleyball title.
articles.body:
LAKELAND — It could have gone the other way — or at least gone down to the wire in five sets. All Saints' come-from-behind rally in the third set was nearly for naught as Tampa Bay HEAT rallied and had set point.

All Saints, however, hung tough, won three consecutive points then finished off the Heat in four sets, 21-25, 25-15, 26-24, 25-9, in the championship match of the Class 1A, District 9 volleyball tournament at All Saints.

The victory gave All Saints its fourth consecutive district title and sends the Saints into Tuesday's regional quarterfinals. The Saints had defeated Tampa Bay HEAT during the regular season and was the top seed in the district.

"It was really important for me (to win district title)," All Saints junior Hali Vatikiotis said. "I love this team and having won four in a row, that's a really big thing. But the main thing is just doing this together as a team with these coaches. I love this team and to be able learn it and go each step of the way and have all of us do it together as a team, that's my main thing because it's not just me. It's not just one person on this team. It's all of us, and that's what makes it special. We get to do it together."

It certainly isn't one person, but Vatikiotis certainly was a big part of it. The team's leader with 227 kills for the season going into the match, she lead All Saints with 20 kills, consistently coming up with big kills at key moments. She also had 11 digs and two aces.

"She's our top outside, great hitter, great leader as well, very consistent whenever she's in the zone," All Saints junior Michael Zavolas said. "But it's all about her leadership as well. She controls a lot of the energy and effort."

Vatikiotis was serving in the third set when All Saints rallied to take the lead after being down 16-11. The Saints went on to take a 23-21 lead and appeared to be on the verge of going up a set.

The Heat, however, rallied and had set point at 24-23.

Gallery: All Saints in volleyball action in 1A-9 district tournament

All Saints survived when Kendall Boardman then put up a spike that was blocked out of bounds. The Saints then won the next to points to take the set then dominated the final set.

"It was great," Vatikiotis said. "It was definitely a turning point for that fourth set that we played. It was really important to get that set and going back and forth and being able to come out and win was really important."

Unlike the first meeting between the two teams when All Saints won in three sets, the Saints dropped the first match.

"We had to fight back, but I don't think any of us were scared," Vatikiotis said. "We just wanted to fight back more."

As she noted, the victory was a team effort and there were plenty of contributions, starting with setter Paige Lenderman. All Saints began the season in a 6-2 attack with Lenderman, who can play anywhere on the court, being one of the two setters and also playing right-side hitter. After an injury during the season, the Saints switched to a 5-1 attack with Lenderman being the primary setter. She did a masterful job Thursday in mixing up the attack and finished with 50 assists.

"Paige is by far one of the best setters in the county," Zavolas said. "She is up there. She controls the tempo of the game. She's a quarterback and she runs it well."

Lenderman mixed it up the sets with Vatikiotis and Sophia Kelly, who had 17 kills and four aces. Alina Varela in the middle had nine kills and four blocks, and Boardman had five kills. Libero Valeria Castro had 19 digs.

So what's next for All Saints in the playoffs? All Saints was the No. 3 seed in the region last year and lost in the regional semifinals to Keswick Christian.

This year, All Saints, ranked No. 4 in Class 1A overall, went into the district tournament ranked No. 2 in its region behind Naples Seacrest Country Day, which was a state semifinalist last year.

"We've got a good shot," Zavolas said. "We've got a good shot in regionals."

articles.summary: Courtland Sutton was held to 19 yards on two receptions by the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6.

Denver Broncos WR Courtland Sutton had two catches (on three targets) for 19 yards in Week 6 versus the Seattle Seahawks .

Why It Matters: Sutton's dismal start to the 2026 campaign continued on Thursday night with a 2-19-0 line, giving the veteran wideout 13 catches, 123 yards, and one touchdown combined this season. articles.title: Winnipeg Jets’ Neal Pionk Is Stepping Up Without Josh Morrissey
articles.summary: The Winnipeg Jets desperately needed a blueliner to step up and fill Josh Morrissey’s shoes. Neal Pionk has taken the mantle.With Morrissey slated to miss so...
articles.body:
The Winnipeg Jets desperately needed a blueliner to step up and fill Josh Morrissey's shoes. Neal Pionk has taken the mantle.

With Morrissey slated to miss some time, Pionk looks like the next man up. Despite losing 4-3 in overtime to the Chicago Blackhawks, Pionk was a big reason Winnipeg stayed in the game.

With the Jets down 2-0 to Chicago, Pionk scored at the 16:57 mark of the first period. Brad Lambert made the play happen when he pulled off a wicked move to keep possession of the puck at the top of the right circle.

Lambert fired the puck, which got deflected and went into the end boards. Morgan Barron collected the puck and found Pionk near the right circle. Pionk blasted the puck through traffic and found twine, cutting Chicago's lead to one goal.

He also had an assist on Kyle Connor's power-play goal at the 4:44 mark of the second period. In the third period, he helped Alex Iafallo score the game-tying goal that ultimately forced overtime.

Pionk Is Turning Into The Jets' Go-To Defenseman

Someone had to step up when Josh Morrissey went down. Pionk now has five points and a goal in his last two games (two assists vs. the Minnesota Wild ). Following Thursday night's loss, Pionk has six points and a goal in seven games.

That puts him on an 84-game pace to snag career numbers if it continues. He would end the year with 12 goals and 72 points. While he probably won't be that productive all season, it's not unrealistic to believe Pionk will snag between 40 and 45 points.

Pionk hit a career-high of 45 points in 71 games in 2019-20. He also had 39 points in 69 games in 2024-25. That said, Pionk is more than capable of being the go-to blueliner in the offensive zone — especially when Winnipeg's top-scoring blueliner is missing time with an injury.

Neal Pionk And Josh Morrissey Could Ultimately Forge A Lethal Combo

While Morrissey is shelved for the foreseeable future, Pionk must keep emulating the heroics that he has achieved over Winnipeg's previous two contests. Once Morrissey is good to go, he and Pionk could make lives miserable for opponents.

It would force opponents to account for two very good two-way defensemen who are always a threat to create scoring chances. For a team that has a so-so 21 goals in seven contests, more productivity on the blue line is needed.

Then, there is the fact that the Jets don't have a star goaltender like Connor Hellebuyck to rely on. Hellebuyck had routinely limited opponents' scoring. While Stuart Skinner and Clay Stevenson have been serviceable, they won't match Hellebuyck's consistency.

Now, the challenge for Pionk is simple: Keep laying good hockey in the offensive zone. Pionk will get another crack at it on Saturday in a dramatic fashion as the Winnipeg Jets will host the defending Stanley Cup Champion, the Carolina Hurricanes .

Should Pionk string together a few more games like he's had vs. Minnesota and against Chicago, he will force teams to account for him.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola shares positive update on Hugo Ekitike and Conor Bradley
articles.summary: Liverpool injury update: Conor Bradley closing in, Hugo Ekitike progressing, Giovanni Leoni suffers setbackLiverpool finally have some clarity on three injur...
articles.body:
Liverpool injury update: Conor Bradley closing in, Hugo Ekitike progressing, Giovanni Leoni suffers setback

Liverpool finally have some clarity on three injured players, and the headline is straightforward. Conor Bradley is close to rejoining parts of first-team training, Hugo Ekitike is moving as expected in his recovery, and Giovanni Leoni has hit an unwelcome bump in the road.

Bradley has been out since January, when he suffered a serious knee injury late in the 0-0 draw with Arsenal. There has been little detail on the precise damage, although it is understood he avoided ligament trouble. For Liverpool, that always mattered. A long lay-off is one thing, structural damage is another.

Conor Bradley nearing Liverpool training return

Andoni Iraola offered the clearest update yet on the right-back's condition. "They are both doing very well," Iraola said. "I think they are in a good place. Conor is not so far from training with the group – not like full training but doing some things with the group.

"Hugo is a little bit behind that but that was always the plan. He is still doing very well according to the plan."

That tells you where things stand. Bradley is not back, but he is close enough to begin integration work. After an absence this long, that is the stage that matters.

Ekitike's situation is more severe and always was. He ruptured his Achilles tendon in April, an injury that demands patience and usually wipes out any temptation to rush. His work between Kirkby and the United States with a specialist suggests Liverpool are taking the obvious route, careful, methodical, no shortcuts.

Iraola was not interested in promises. "It's difficult (to put a timescale on them both). When they have been injured for so long it's difficult to say but I think Conor is not very far from starting doing things with us."

Leoni's case is separate and unfortunate. Signed from Parma last summer, he suffered an ACL injury on debut, about as cruel a start as it gets. Iraola has now confirmed a setback, though the expectation remains that he could return to training around the next international break.

For Liverpool, this is where the medical department earns its keep. Bradley is the nearest, Ekitike is on schedule, and Leoni still needs careful handling. That is the reality, plain and simple.

articles.title: What Seahawks QB Sam Darnold said after throwing away OT loss to Broncos with brutal INT
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks clawed their way back into Thursday night’s game against the Denver Broncos, only to watch it slip away on one throw. Sam Darnold did n...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks clawed their way back into Thursday night's game against the Denver Broncos, only to watch it slip away on one throw . Sam Darnold did not try to dress it up afterward.

"There's no way to sugarcoat it, that one sucked," Darnold said after the game . Seattle fell 17-14 in overtime at Empower Field at Mile High, dropping the defending Super Bowl champions to 3-3 on the season.

The Seahawks trailed 14-3 in the fourth quarter before mounting a comeback. George Holani punched in a rushing touchdown, and Rashid Shaheed caught the two-point conversion to make it a three-point game. A field goal then tied it at 14 and sent the game to overtime.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Seattle received the ball first in overtime, but the possession went sideways almost immediately. A holding penalty on the kickoff return pushed the Seahawks back to their own 11-yard line. On a third-and-7, Darnold threw an interception to Broncos cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian , handing Denver the ball at the Seattle 43.

The Broncos did little with the short field, but they did not need to. Wil Lutz drilled a 53-yard field goal to end it .

The timing made it especially painful. Seattle had just erased an 11-point deficit on the road, and one throw turned a potential statement win into a loss.

It was Darnold's second interception of the night. Kris Abrams-Draine also picked him off late in regulation. Darnold finished 27-of-51 passing for 278 yards, and he struggled badly early, completing just seven of 15 attempts for 52 yards in the first half.

Denver's defense was relentless throughout , finishing with five sacks and three takeaways despite playing without star cornerback Patrick Surtain II and safety Talanoa Hufanga.

The loss stings for a team coming off a championship. Darnold led Seattle to a Super Bowl LX title in February, beating the New England Patriots 29-13, and the Seahawks opened this season with a 13-10 win over New England in a rematch.

Now Seattle sits at .500 and will need its quarterback to bounce back quickly. Darnold's blunt assessment suggests he knows exactly how costly the mistake was , and he did not hide from it. His 51 pass attempts also show how heavily Seattle leaned on him to carry the offense in Denver.

articles.summary: The San Francisco Giants had a disappointing season after posting a 65-97 record. They had the second-worst record in the National League. The Milwaukee Brew...
articles.body:
The San Francisco Giants had a disappointing season after posting a 65-97 record. They had the second-worst record in the National League.

The Milwaukee Brewers, on the other hand, swept the Los Angeles Dodgers in the best-of-seven National League Championship Series.

The Brewers beat the Dodgers 6-4 in Game 4 of the NLCS on Thursday.

Ex-Giants Pitcher Headed to World Series

Former Giants pitcher Kyle Harrison made the Brewers' postseason roster. Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy decided to keep the left-handed pitcher despite a rocky second half of the season.

However, the Brewers did not plan to utilize Harrison as a starting pitcher. Instead, he was added to give the NLCS champs another lefty arm out of the bullpen who could provide length.

Harrison has not yet made an appearance in the postseason for the Brewers.

He last pitched 2 innings in a regular-season game against the St. Louis Cardinals on Sep. 26.

How Did Kyle Harrison End Up on the Brewers?

Harrison was a key piece in the Giants' blockbuster trade for Rafael Devers in June of the 2025 season.

The left-handed pitcher was dealt to the Boston Red Sox along with RHP Jordan Hicks, outfield prospect James Tibbs III, and pitching prospect Jose Bello.

But Harrison's career in Boston was short-lived. He pitched only 12 innings over 3 games before the 24-year-old was dealt again.

The Red Sox traded Harrison, infielder David Hamilton, and LHP prospect Shane Drohan to the Brewers in February in exchange for infielders Caleb Durbin, Andruw Monasterio, and Anthony Seigler.

The former Giants top pitching prospect helped guide the Brewers to a 103-59 regular-season record in 2026.

Kyle Harrison Impressed in First Season With Brewers

Harrison jumped to an incredible start with the Brewers. The starting pitcher held a 7-1 record with a 1.57 ERA through his first 11 starts.

In his appearance against the Giants on June 2, Harrison pitched 5 2/3 innings, tallied 12 strikeouts, and gave up 1 earned run. The Brewers beat the Giants 8-3.

However, Harrison struggled and dealt with left forearm tightness in the latter half of the season in Milwaukee.

The left-handed pitcher finished the regular season with an 11-5 record and 4.20 ERA.

Looking Back at Kyle Harrison's Career With the Giants

Harrison was one of the best Giants pitching prospects in the organization before he made his MLB debut in 2023.

The starting pitcher made 7 starts and posted a 4.15 ERA in his rookie year.

Harrison then posted a 0.7 WAR season in 2024, making 24 starts and posting a 4.56 ERA. He had a 7-7 record.

The lefty appeared in 11 games for the Giants in 2025 before being traded to the Red Sox.

articles.title: Chiefs’ perfect Jerry Jeudy trade offer to Browns to add help for Patrick Mahomes at trade deadline
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are undefeated. Patrick Mahomes is thriving, and Kenneth Walker III has given the offense a devastating new dimension. Yet even at 4-0...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are undefeated. Patrick Mahomes is thriving, and Kenneth Walker III has given the offense a devastating new dimension. Yet even at 4-0, Kansas City's receiving corps is losing depth at the worst possible time. Tyquan Thornton's dislocated ankle and Rashee Rice's lingering hamstring issue have left Mahomes with fewer reliable options outside Travis Kelce and Xavier Worthy. General manager Brett Veach should take advantage of the team's Week 5 bye to explore a deal for Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy . A 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-rounder would be a reasonable opening offer for him.

Jeudy's situation in Cleveland makes him an intriguing trade target. After earning Pro Bowl honors with 1,229 receiving yards in 2024, he recorded 602 yards in 2025 and has managed just eight receptions for 81 yards through five games this season.

That dip in production does not necessarily mean Jeudy has lost his ability. Cleveland's evolving receiving rotation has limited his opportunities. A change of scenery could give him a chance to rediscover his rhythm. For the Browns, moving him could create additional opportunities for other receivers. It would also bring back draft capital to support their longer-term plans.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

For Kansas City, the appeal is obvious. Jeudy is a polished route-runner who can create separation against man coverage. He can find soft spots against zone defenses and give Mahomes a dependable target on intermediate routes. He would complement Worthy's speed and Kelce's ability to exploit mismatches.

Jeudy also has familiarity with Chiefs wide receivers coach Chad O'Shea. He previously worked with him in Cleveland. That connection could help ease the transition into Eric Bieniemy's offense. Of course, learning Kansas City's terminology and timing would still require work.

The ideal offer would see Kansas City send Cleveland a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round selection in exchange for Jeudy. That package would give the Browns two future assets without forcing the Chiefs to surrender a premium pick or a key contributor from their current roster .

The fourth-round selection would be the centerpiece. The sixth-rounder would also provide additional compensation for a receiver with a Pro Bowl season on his résumé. Cleveland might prefer a higher pick. However, Jeudy's limited production in 2026 makes a mid-round package a defensible starting point.

Kansas City must also evaluate the financial implications before finalizing a deal. Jeudy carries a contract that runs through 2027. His future cap hit would need to fit into the Chiefs' plans. The Browns could potentially absorb a portion of the remaining salary, but that would have to be negotiated rather than assumed.

Veach should resist overpaying simply because the team is undefeated. The Chiefs have built sustained success by balancing aggressive moves with disciplined roster management. If Cleveland demands a second-round pick, Kansas City should explore alternatives.

Kansas City's 4-0 start has been built on balance. Walker has delivered explosive rushing production. Mahomes has produced timely plays. The offensive line has helped the team control the tempo of games. Still, injuries can quickly undermine that balance, particularly when defenses begin concentrating their attention on the remaining healthy playmakers.

Jeudy could give Bieniemy another versatile option in the passing game. His route-running would help Mahomes find quick answers against pressure. His ability to separate over the middle could punish defenses that devote extra attention to Worthy or Kelce.

The timing is important, too. Kansas City's bye provides an opportunity to integrate a new receiver before the schedule becomes more demanding. A deal completed early enough would give Jeudy additional practice time to build chemistry with Mahomes and learn the offense.

Kansas City's standing pat would be a gamble given the current injury situation. Jeudy offers a reasonable blend of experience, route-running ability, and potential upside. These make him a worthwhile target if Cleveland is prepared to discuss a deal.

A fourth-round pick and a sixth-rounder would give the Browns future assets. It would also allow the Chiefs to preserve their most valuable draft capital. The financial details would matter, and Veach should walk away if the price becomes excessive.

Mahomes gives Kansas City a championship opportunity every season. The front office's responsibility is to give him enough dependable weapons to maximize it. If Jeudy becomes available at the right price, the Chiefs should pursue him before another contender gets the chance.

articles.title: UW Opponent Defensive Preview: Purdue Boilermakers
articles.summary: The Huskies hit the road this week and head to West Lafayette, IN to take on the Purdue Boilermakers in search of their first conference win. Washington (3-3...
articles.body:
The Huskies hit the road this week and head to West Lafayette, IN to take on the Purdue Boilermakers in search of their first conference win. Washington (3-3, 0-3) are in the midst of a three game skid that began during conference play Purdue (3-3, 2-1) on the other hand are a program that found its footing and positive momentum over the last two weeks with its first two conference wins since 2023, beating Illinois and blowing out a Minnesota squad that manhandled UW on Montlake. Purdue's new found success has largely been driven by it's strides on offense, but with the Huskies struggling on offense and starting Elijah Brown at QB for the first time, it's anybody's best guess as to how this match up will go down.

At a glance, Purdue's defense is still a liability. Averaging 31 points allowed (119th), 243 passing yards allowed (113th), and 157 rushing yards allowed (93rd) per game, the Boilermakers rank near the bottom of the FBS in standard statistical defensive performance. However, those stats are skewed dramatically by 52-pt, 49-pt, and 38-pt performances against UCLA, Notre Dame, and Wake Forest earlier in the season. In their last two games, they've only allowed 17 and 13 points to Illinois and Minnesota where they held Minnesota to just 2.1 yards per carry and Illinois to 6.1 yards per pass.

With just 7 sacks and 5 turnovers on the season, Purdue's defense hasn't relied on splash plays as much as steady down-to-down play. Plays are funneled to active LBs and DBs such as Charles Correa, Jojo Hayden, and John Slaughter, who are among the team's leading tacklers. Keeping them clean and forcing opponents into one-dimensional play calling help these second and third level defenders in play making mode.

If UW's offense is going to turn it's season around, it needs to build on the momentum that Elijah Brown found in the second half of the Iowa game. Brown's on-time passing and reduction of negative plays seemed to provide a spark to the offense that Demond Williams couldn't provide prior to his injury. At this point, we shouldn't expect any sort of run game resurgence, but if we aren't able to muster at least a serviceable run game that can complement a pass-centric game plan, we're not going to find much success against any opponent. Brown did show himself to be a much better distributor of the ball, and was able to consistently target the middle of the field. If he can continue to do so against Purdue, the horizontal stress from the passing game may assist in softening up the box for the run game to find some traction.

articles.title: Rossi vs Verstappen: Everything to know about their historic GT3 battle
articles.summary: Two of the greatest figures in motorsport history will face off this weekend - and no, it’s not a gimmick. Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen will b...
articles.body:
Two of the greatest figures in motorsport history will face off this weekend - and no, it's not a gimmick.

Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen will be racing against nine-time motorcycle world champion Valentino Rossi in what sounds like a social media bit.

Yet this isn't a social media stunt, far from it, as they face off on four wheels in the GT World Challenge Europe finale in Portimao, Portugal.

Verstappen will be making his debut in the series but has already wowed in a handful of endurance appearances alongside his F1 exploits.

He also enters in form, having won his first race of the season in Malaysia; he went back-to-back with a victory in Singapore last time out.

Rossi, meanwhile, is no stranger to GT3, having taken to four-wheeled racing after retiring from MotoGP in 2021.

Which teams are Rossi and Verstappen racing for?

Rossi will be driving a BMW M4 GT3 for the Belgian outfit Team WRT. The car has worn his legendary blue and luminous yellow number 46 for the last three years and will be impossible to miss in Portugal.

He will be sharing the car with German Max Hesse and American Neil Verhagen.

Verstappen may have had unsuccessful talks with Mercedes in F1, but he's still working with them in endurance racing. The Dutchman will be driving a Mercedes-AMG GT3 under his own Verstappen Racing team branding.

Verstappen will race alongside British pair Ben Barnicoat and Chris Lulham.

Rossi's trademark colours are unmissable (Photo: Race Pictures)

Rossi took to four wheels regularly throughout his motorcycle career, testing for Ferrari in F1 and winning the Monza Rally Show on five occasions.

He's been with Team WRT since 2022 and has been part of the GT World Challenge Sprint Cup-winning team an impressive three times.

On top of that, the 47-year-old has been a runner-up in the Gulf 12 Hours and finished third in this year's Intercontinental GT Challenge.

Verstappen made his endurance debut in 2025 and was part of the team that took the Gold Cup victory at the 24 Hours of Spa.

Earlier this year, he took part in the Nurburgring 24 Hours and led after a mega start until a driveshaft failure took the team out of the race.

What have Rossi and Verstappen said about racing each other?

Speaking about the prospect of facing Verstappen, Rossi said: "It's going to be incredible. It will be a big challenge because he's sure to be incredibly fast, but it will be fantastic.

"I have to admit I never imagined I would end up competing against Max Verstappen . It will be fantastic for everyone to have him there, and I hope to have the opportunity to follow him and see how he drives."

Verstappen commented: "I hope to have the opportunity to see him. He's a very interesting guy, so I hope I can catch up with him.

"I hope I don't see him during the race, because normally that would be a good sign.

"Actually, I hope not to see anyone, to be ahead of everyone and do a good job. But you never know. The grid is very competitive, so I'm looking forward to the challenge."

"I hope I don't see him during the race, because normally that would be a good sign."

When is Rossi vs Verstappen? Full Portimao race schedule

Paid practice took place on Thursday in which Verstappen got an outing on the Portimao track he loves that will be back on the F1 calendar next season.

Where can you watch Rossi vs Verstappen live for free?

The race will be streamed live for free on the GT World YouTube channel, while Sky Sports in the UK will also host their own coverage.

Which F1 and GT3 stars will race against Rossi and Verstappen?

Nicki Thiim (Aston Martin), Mirko Bortolotti (Lamborghini), and Thomas Preining (Porsche) are all huge names in the world of endurance racing, and Rossi and Verstappen will have to be at their best to beat them.

Charles Leclerc's younger brother Arthur will be racing for AF Corse, while former Haas F1 driver Nikita Mazepin will be racing for Team Motopark Mercedes-AMG.

articles.title: WNBA Finals predictions 2026: Sporting News projects Dream vs. Valkyries championship series
articles.summary: The field is down to two — will Angel Reese and the Dream win the 2026 WNBA Finals, or will Gabby Williams and the Valkyries win a franchise first? The Sport...
articles.body:
The WNBA playoffs have been filled with drama, from the first No. 8 seed to knock off a No. 1 seed and Caitlin Clark suffering an early exit , to A'ja Wilson and the defending champion Aces being ousted in the semifinals. Now, it's down to just the Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries .

The Dream needed just one season with Angel Reese to reach the finals for the first time since 2013. Brought over in an offseason trade with the Chicago Sky , Reese has been everything the team needed and more. She earned Defensive Player of the Year honors after leading the WNBA in rebounds per game and blocks per game, becoming a dominant force in Atlanta's frontcourt. Along with the former LSU sensation, Rhyne Howard, Allisha Gray and postseason breakout star Jordin Canada are leading the charge on an offense averaging 92.6 points per game during the postseason.

On the other side of the court is one of the biggest surprises in the WNBA this season. In just their second year in the league, the Valkyries went from a sneaky No. 8 seed in their inaugural season to fighting for the No. 1 seed in the league. Gabby Williams may be the face of the franchise, but it's a complete team effort in Golden State, with Sixth Player of the Year Janelle Saluan and Veronica Burton playing key roles in the team's success.

Both teams come into the WNBA Finals with momentum. Atlanta has yet to lose a game this postseason, sweeping the Washington Mystics in the quarterfinals before rolling over the No. 8 seed New York Liberty in three games to advance to the finals. On the other side, Golden State has one blemish on its postseason record, needing a Game 3 to defeat the pesky Dallas Wings before a 3-0 sweep over the Las Vegas Aces .

Neither franchise has won a WNBA title, but that is guaranteed to change this year. The question is, who will it be — the Dream, who have waited nearly 20 years to lift a championship trophy, or the young Valkyries franchise closing in on the ultimate prize in just their second WNBA campaign?

The Sporting News is giving out its expert predictions for the 2026 WNBA Finals.

WNBA Finals winner prediction: Dream over Valkyries

WNBA Finals MVP prediction: Angel Reese, Dream

I'm stubbornly sticking with the Atlanta Dream. The only thing that really scares me is if Allisha Gray isn't available for the series, or if she plays but can't impact the game at her usual level. The Valks have proven they can shut down the league's best offenses, so the Dream will need all hands on deck. But while most of the attention has gone to how great Golden State is defensively — best defensive rating in the regular season — the Dream have a lockdown defense of their own. Atlanta finished the regular season with the third-best defense in the W, and going into the Finals series, it's Atlanta that boasts the best defense so far in the playoffs.

The league's Defensive Player of the Year, Angel Reese, has been the key cog in that all season long and if the Dream can pull off four more wins, it'll be because Reese is once again the most impactful player on the floor. Crown ATL Barbie and the Dream in six.

The Dream are winning the 2026 Finals. Their 30-14 record heading into the playoffs, good for the No.4 seed, may not seem all that impressive. But this is a team that showed championship potential in the games where they were on. They've put it all together at the right time, winning 10 straight, including playoff sweeps against the Mystics and Liberty. Angel Reese has led the charge, showing why she was the league's Defensive Player of the Year.

Reese is the biggest star in this matchup. She has upped her game during the playoffs. Her rim protection, scoring, and shooting have all markedly improved through the first two rounds. She brings a high motor and generational rebounding skill to the table every night. If the Dream win, it will be behind continued brilliant performances from her.

WNBA Finals winner prediction: Valkyries over Dream

WNBA Finals MVP prediction: Gabby Williams, Valkyries

The WNBA Finals will end with a former Chicago Sky lottery pick and NCAA champion who is known as one of the best defensive players in the league and has made an indelible mark in her first season with a new team. Of course, I'm referring to Gabby Williams. The Valkryies leading scorer, who finished second in DPOY voting behind Angel Reese, enters the WNBA Finals having scored more points this postseason than anyone not named A'ja Wilson. Williams faces a tall task on both ends of the floor, leading a balanced Golden State attack while spearheading the point of attack against Atlanta's prolific backcourt of Allisha Gray, Jordin Canada and Rhyne Howard. Reese might be the biggest name, but the Valkyries are favored and if they win, all signs point towards strong two-end play from Williams.

The WNBA Finals will end with a former Chicago Sky lottery pick and NCAA champion, who is known as one of the best defensive players in the league and has made an indelible mark in her first season with a new team, hosting the WNBA Finals MVP trophy.

WNBA Finals MVP prediction: Jordin Canada, Dream

I'm all in on the Dream winning this year's WNBA Finals. This team plays with such ferocity that I think even the Valkyries will struggle defensively. This series won't be another sweep, that's for sure, but I think Atlanta's ability to go after each possession like it's the last will lead it to its first WNBA title. As for MVP? I'm going with Jordin Canada. She not only leads the Dream in points and rebounds this postseason, but she knows how to come up clutch in crucial moments.

Cate Schiller, Global Content Coordinator

As a Bay Area native, I have to go with the Valkyries here. Golden State has shown such discipline and poise in these Playoffs, rising to the moment to dismantle giants like Las Vegas with relative ease. With ample star power and a bench adding 32.3 points per game, the Valks should outlast the Dream, especially if they're without Allisha Gray.

This series will be an undeniable shootout, but I believe Golden State has what it takes to make history and bring a title back to the Bay — and if they do, Gabby Williams will be MVP.

I've gone back and forth over who will win the WNBA Finals. This series has all the makings of a slugfest: it's a matchup of the league's top two defenses and two of the league's top coaches in Natalie Nakase and Karl Smesko. In any case, I don't expect it to end before Game 6. The Valkyries can go 11 players deep and they play the best defense the WNBA has seen in at least half a decade. But Golden State hasn't seen an offense that plays at Atlanta's pace. And the Dream's defense — anchored by the literal DPOY — is every bit as imposing.

"Make-or-miss league" is horribly cliched, but in this case, I think the Dream simply will make more shots than the Valkyries. And with respect to the outstanding Gabby Williams, Atlanta has this series' single best player in Reese, who has a history of elevating her game when the lights are brightest. I think Atlanta in 6, and Reese as Finals MVP. She's averaging 18-8-4 stocks through five playoff games. If her shot remains consistent against the Golden State defense, her MVP case will speak for itself.

Before the playoffs, it may have been hard to picture a WNBA Finals without either the Minnesota Lynx or the Las Vegas Aces, but here we are. The Dream head into this series as victors of their last 10 games, a span that includes the regular season and playoffs. A Golden State team that finished 2026 as the No. 1-ranked team with the lowest opponent PPG (75.1), FG% (41.4%), and 3P% (32.6%) also took all three of their regular-season games against the Dream. That being said, Atlanta is my pick to win the series. They have fewer question marks about scoring, and they've consistently been able to cash in when they force turnovers (72 points off 45 NY Liberty turnovers in the semifinals).

Angel Reese has shown tremendous progression this season. She's already won the Defensive Player of the Year award, and now she'll win Finals MVP. Her rebounding has always been a talking point throughout her career, but her scoring leading up to the Finals has shown she's taken the next step in becoming one of the best players in the league. Now, she can show that on the biggest stage.
