articles.title: Jayden Daniels makes it clear how he feels about Dan Quinn
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels wants everyone to know how much he appreciates Dan Quinn.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels met with the media on Thursday and took full accountability for Sunday's end-of-game gaffe against the New York Giants that cost the team a win. Instead of improving to 2-3, Washington tied with the Giants and sits at 1-3-1 heading into Week 6.

"Just going back and reflecting on it and, you know, sitting back and ultimately, I know it's a lot of he say or whatever you're trying to make, but ultimately, like, it's on me at the end," Daniels said. "I know DQ is getting a lot of slack for it or whatever, you know, but regardless of what happens, I'm the person on the field that's supposed to calm everything, control everything, and I failed to the standard I told myself to and the standard in this organization. So, it's just something for me to move on. Not saying I'm proud of it or anything. Obviously, looking back, like, it could have resulted in a loss; we tied, but it was a fail in my eyes, and, you know, I know I'm better than that. I hold myself to a higher standard than that."

Daniels's statement was excellent and shows why he's considered such an outstanding leader. One part that stood out was his acknowledgment of what head coach Dan Quinn has gone through this week. Some in the media and among fans have called for Quinn's job, which is ridiculous. If you want to criticize Quinn for his record, that's understandable, but jumping on a soapbox to call for his job over Sunday's end-of-game debacle was foolish.

Daniels later explained what it meant to him that Quinn took the heat for Sunday's debacle.

"I mean, that's just the person he is, you know, the type of person that he is and obviously, you know, all eyes are on him, all eyes are on me," Daniels said. "And regardless of how people talk about him, we love DQ here. You know, I appreciate him. I always say that for making my dreams come true of being a starting quarterback in the NFL. And, you know, he helped me with the opportunity, so, super blessed to have DQ, and, you know, he means a lot to me."

If you had any doubt about how Washington's locker room will respond to Quinn, you shouldn't have any longer. Does that mean the Commanders will go out and upset the 49ers on Monday night? Of course not. But this team won't quit on Quinn. When he talks culture and character, that's what he's talking about. His team is built to respond to adversity and lean on one another in tough times.

Daniels and Quinn have maintained a close relationship since they both arrived in Washington in 2024. That relationship is closer than ever because of the difficult times they've faced together.

articles.title: Liverpool take giant step closer to Sergi Altimira
articles.summary: Liverpool are taking a step closer to signing Sergi Altimira or the next best thing. The Reds have shifted their plans.We've written this week that Liverpool...
articles.body:
Liverpool are taking a step closer to signing Sergi Altimira or the next best thing. The Reds have shifted their plans.

We've written this week that Liverpool are in the market for a new midfielder and that Sergi Altimira is on their radar. Anfield Watch and he might just be who they move for in 2027.

And that would be a fine move. Altimira is a really interesting player and one who our Value Adder model suggests held the highest defensive value per 90 minutes across the top five leagues last season.

Sporting certainly believed that. They moved to sign Altimira from Real Betis in the summer, replacing the outgoing Morten Hjulumnd, who signed for Atlético Madrid.

We think they've made an upgrade there - and it's drawn the attention of Liverpool. More than that, we think they're making true preparations to sign him.

Sergi Altimira is suddenly a perfect fit

We had real questions over the interest in Altimira. He is about as 'defensive midfielder' as it gets - tall, large turning circle, not particularly fast, and not one other consistently burst forward.

This flies in the face of everything Liverpool have produced in midfield for two years. The Reds have basically just used attacking midfielders, defiantly sticking with their philosophy even when they can't control a midfield and are losing game after game because of it.

Altimira's display against RC Lens this week, for instance, was the opposite. He sat at the base of a midfield three and spent large portions of the second half between split centre-backs. It's the Fabinho role at Liverpool - and one it appears they'd done away with.

However, Andoni Iraola is opening the door again. He's played with a sitting midfielder in each of his last two fixtures here, with Alexis Mac Allister doing it against Manchester City and Trey Nyoni against LASK.

Such a system means Altimira is a lot more likely to join as Liverpool suddenly do use a player in his role. And considering his numbers last season and this term, there aren't many better at it.

articles.title: Cruz Castillo's last-minute touchdown caps Brackenridge rally to beat Burbank
articles.summary: The running back rumbled into the end zone with 37 seconds left in the game to give the Eagles their first lead of the game and notch an important victory.
articles.body:
Joshua Garcia threw for two second-half scores and Cruz Castillo scored with 37 seconds remaining as Brackenridge rallied for a 21-14 win over Burbank on Thursday at SAISD Sports Complex.

Castillo's game-winning 28-yard touchdown run capped off a Brackenridge comeback in which the Eagles scored 21 unanswered points after falling behind 14-0 in the third quarter.

Brackenridge (5-2, 3-2) won its third game in a row, at least temporarily moving into sole possesion of fourth place in District 14-5A-II and putting itself in a position to earn its first playoff berth in five years. Brackenridge next meets Jefferson, which entered Week 8 tied with Eagles for the fourth playoff spot, next Friday at 7 p.m. at SAISD Sports Complex.

"We're a second-half team, and the kids know that," Brackenridge coach Steve Garcia said. "Our goal is to play good four quarters, and we haven't yet. At the most we've done is three great quarters, but we are a second-half team. The kids, they love the second half, and we always preach 0-0. It's literally 0-0 (at halftime), let's go out there and make some stops and we're going to win this ball game."

It didn't happen right away. After the slow, scoreless first half, Burbank (1-6, 1-4) took a 14-0 lead late in the third quarter thanks to a 34-yard touchdown run from Bryan Jalomo and a Christian Gutierrez 43-yard scoop-and-score.

But Castillo got it going for Brackenridge in the second half, as the senior running back finished with 141 yards on 28 carries. On his game-clinching touchdown, Castillo refused to go down, bouncing off a tackler before breaking to the outside to the end zone.

"I was just looking for the open lane, the linemen did a good job," Castillo said. "And I was like, 'You know what, let me just play physical' and that's what I did. I just bounced off one guy and I saw the open lane and I just went for it."

Joshua Garcia, the backup sophomore quarterback who has stepped in for the injured Ahmir Thompson, was in awe of Castillo's running style.

"Cruz is something else," Joshua Garcia said. "I've never seen anything like him, just a hard runner, dedicated, determined. He's just one of a kind." Brackenridge started its comeback with over two minutes left in the third quarter, when Joshua Garcia connected with Daniel Rincon on a 50-yard touchdown pass to cut the lead to 14-7.

Brackenridge defensive lineman Pedro Canizales Sanchez recovered a fumbled Burbank snap to set up the Eagles' next score, a 7-yard touchdown pass from Joshua Garcia to Damien Castro Diaz, who twisted to make a diving catch, tying the score at 14 with 6:45 left in the fourth quarter.

It was the second win a row for Brackenridge with Joshua Garcia at quarterback. After a rough start, Garcia finished with 108 yards on 10-of-18 passing, with an interception and two touchdowns.

"Definitely, getting more comfortable," Joshua Garcia said of having to step in the starting role. "Definitely doing what I'm told to do. Doing my job, getting comfortable back there and doing my thing."

Brackenridge won the turnover battle with two interceptions and a fumble recovery, while Burbank forced two turnovers, an interception and the Gutierrez fumble recovery that led to a score.
